agents.name: orchestrator
agents.mission: Break down requests into package-owned work and coordinate handoffs.
rules: Prefer one owner per task.
Define contracts before implementation when a change spans packages.
Require handoff summaries before merge.

agents.name: web-ui-canvas
agents.mission: Build and improve the canvas-first web experience.
ownership: route handlers in the web app
rules: Do not put database logic in React components.
Do not put AI orchestration logic in UI unless it is a thin client call.
Keep canvas state serializable and version-friendly.
Avoid demo-only shortcuts in production paths.
Preserve existing design language unless the task requires a redesign.
output: API or contract needs from other agents

agents.name: ai-prompt-engine
agents.mission: Build deterministic prompt logic for landscape and garden design.
rules: Keep prompt assembly deterministic where possible.
Never erase layout constraints for aesthetic reasons.
Build outputs that can be audited and versioned.
Use shared types for prompt inputs and outputs when available.

agents.name: db-security
agents.mission: Own schema, RLS, Supabase types, and server-side data access patterns.
rules: Never trust user_id, owner_id, or project_id from the client.
Verify authenticated user before reading or mutating data.
Enable RLS for all user-owned tables before production.
Keep storage private by default.
Prefer stable storage paths over long-lived signed URLs.
Prevent cross-user access to projects, assets, chat messages, snapshots, jobs, and exports.

agents.name: queue-worker
agents.mission: Own async jobs, queue contracts, and background processors.
rules: Keep job payloads serializable and versioned.
Avoid embedding UI concerns in job contracts.
Track job type, user ID, project ID, input snapshot, inputs, prompt reference, status, error, outputs.
Do not log secrets, tokens, signed URLs, or private paths.
output: retry and failure behavior if relevant

agents.name: shared-contracts
agents.mission: Own shared types, constants, enums, and reusable helpers.
rules: Keep shared code framework-agnostic.
Avoid importing server-only modules into shared code.
Keep naming stable and explicit.
Prefer small, composable types over broad utility dumping grounds.

agents.name: qa-integration
rules: Review changed files and contract boundaries.
Verify that no package leaked into the wrong layer.
Check for missing tests or risky assumptions.
If a command cannot be run, explain why and what risk remains.
